2608.27102.title: LAAF: A Layered Accountability Architecture Framework for LLM Applications
2608.27102.paper_summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) operate in hospitals, courtrooms, banks, and public service desks, where fluent, confident outputs are treated as authoritative even when ungrounded or incorrect. When such an output contributes to harm, who is answerable, and through what mechanisms can responsibility be traced, explained, and acted upon? Following PRISMA guidance, five databases were searched from January 2022 to March 2026 against four review questions; of 4,512 records identified, 122 primary studies were included, together with 12 regulatory and standards documents analysed as primary sources. The review consolidates a sociotechnical account of accountability as an actor-forum relation resolved into five dimensions, and synthesises mechanisms across four families: technical controls, human oversight, organisational governance, and documentation and traceability, each with a maturity assessment. The corpus is read through a four-layer classification device spanning provenance, application logic, human oversight, and governance and redress, cross-cut by traceability, role clarity, and continuous monitoring. Both are mapped onto the EU AI Act, whose high-risk obligations have applied since 2 August 2026, the NIST AI RMF with its Generative AI Profile, ISO/IEC 42001, and sectoral guidance in healthcare, consumer finance, education, and the public sector. Four persistent gaps emerge: under-specification of human oversight, absence of shared accountability metrics, disciplinary disconnection, and limited empirical evaluation, alongside five structural tensions that no surveyed instrument resolves. The review closes by consolidating the classification device into an integrated accountability architecture, LAAF, with cybersecurity aligned to the OWASP LLM Top 10 (2025); it is a synthesis of the surveyed evidence rather than a validated artefact.
2608.27102.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）在醫院、法庭、銀行和公共服務櫃檯中運作，流利、自信的輸出即使在缺乏根據或不正確的情況下也被視為權威。當這樣的輸出造成傷害時，誰應負責，責任又能通過什麼機制被追溯、解釋和執行？根據PRISMA指導方針，從2022年1月到2026年3月對四個評審問題進行了五個數據庫的搜索；在識別的4,512條記錄中，納入了122項主要研究，以及12份作為主要來源分析的監管和標準文件。該評審整合了一個社會技術的問責制賬戶，作為一種行為者-論壇關係，分為五個維度，並綜合了四個家庭中的機制：技術控制、人為監督、組織治理，以及文檔和可追溯性，每個都有成熟度評估。該語料庫通過一個涵蓋來源、應用邏輯、人為監督以及治理和救濟的四層分類裝置進行閱讀，並交叉考量可追溯性、角色清晰度和持續監控。這兩者都映射到歐盟人工智慧法案，其高風險義務自2026年8月2日起生效，NIST AI RMF及其生成式AI概況，ISO/IEC 42001，以及在醫療、消費金融、教育和公共部門的行業指導。出現了四個持續的缺口：人為監督的規範不足、缺乏共享的問責指標、學科間的脫節，以及有限的實證評估，還有五個結構性緊張關係，沒有調查的工具能解決。該評審以整合分類裝置為結尾，形成一個綜合的問責架構LAAF，並將網絡安全與OWASP LLM前10名（2025年）對齊；這是一個調查證據的綜合，而不是經過驗證的產物。
